name: Pydantic AI
tagline: A typed, provider-independent Python framework for building agents and working with language models.
hook: A scope-conscious guide to user impact, compatibility, verification, sibling defects, API defaults, and focused local rules.
summary: Pydantic AI tells contributors to protect both the project and its users, then limits scope, compatibility changes, and verification claims. Topic and directory guides hold coding details; broad design principles do not justify broadening a fix.

references.label: Product skills for building Pydantic AI agents

techniques.title: Keep general design philosophy from widening a bug fix
techniques.body: The guide prefers extensible primitives for new designs but explicitly limits a fix to reproduced behavior. Sibling providers or fields enter the patch only after their shared defect has been confirmed.
techniques.quote: Extend a fix to sibling fields, providers, or models only after confirming, by reproducing, that they share the same defect;

techniques.title: Define compatibility through existing behavior
techniques.body: Adding a defaulted parameter is not sufficient if users must pass a new argument to retain what they already had. The guide requires the default to preserve behavior and makes the new behavior opt-in.
techniques.quote: The default must preserve existing behavior; the new behavior is what users opt into

techniques.title: Protect wider APIs from narrow fixes
techniques.body: The file describes product surfaces as nested: users of an adapter or durable engine also use the base Agent. A fix for the narrower layer must not change behavior for unaffected users of the wider one.
techniques.quote: Documenting it doesn't make it acceptable, only expected; if no scoping leaves the wider surface untouched, that's a design question for maintainers, not a docs note.

techniques.title: Reserve process isolation for process-dependent behavior
techniques.body: The test guidance explains the cost of starting another interpreter. It permits subprocesses for CLI, startup, or import isolation while keeping ordinary logic tests in process.
techniques.quote: Reserve subprocesses for behavior that depends on the process boundary, such as CLI invocation, interpreter startup, or import isolation.

techniques.title: Use scoped guides for implementation details
techniques.body: The root file makes the topic index mandatory and then lists directory-specific instructions for models, providers, tools, durable execution, UI, and other areas. The global requirements remain separate from those local mechanics.
techniques.quote: When generating or reviewing code anywhere in this repo, always read [agent_docs/index.md](agent_docs/index.md) and follow/enforce those guidelines.

steal: Require evidence before extending a fix to neighboring implementations.
Define compatibility in terms of unchanged default behavior.
Keep fixes for a narrow integration from affecting a wider API.
Use subprocess tests only when the process boundary matters.
Route implementation work through topic and directory instructions.
outline: Your primary responsibility is to the project and its users
Ensuring the task is ready for implementation
